overview: Elam was one of the oldest civilizations, centered on Susa and the highlands of Anshan in southwestern Iran. Its language belongs to no known family; its kings built ziggurats and fought, traded and intermarried with Mesopotamia for more than two thousand years.

items.text: King Untash-Napirisha built the ziggurat of Chogha Zanbil, the best preserved ziggurat anywhere, with baked-brick stairways and glazed tiles.
Irrigation canals from the Karun and Karkheh rivers watered the Khuzestan plain.
Bronze casting on a large scale: the statue of Queen Napir-Asu from Susa weighs 1,750 kilograms.
Proto-Elamite, one of the earliest scripts, was written on clay at Susa around 3100 BCE and is still undeciphered.
Cylinder seals and rock-cut reliefs of kings and processions, as at Kul-e Farah.
A pantheon headed by Inshushinak, the god of Susa, with the goddess Kiririsha and the highland god Napirisha.
Kingship passed between brothers and nephews, and some scholars read the record as descent through the female line, unusual in the ancient Near East.
Chogha Zanbil was among the first Iranian sites listed by UNESCO.
Elamite was one of the three languages of the Achaemenid royal inscriptions, and Elamite scribes kept the Persepolis archives.

fall.text: Assyria sacked Susa in 647 BCE. The small Elamite kingdoms that followed passed under the Persians of Anshan, and Cyrus's empire, which took Babylon in 539 BCE, made Susa one of its capitals.
